craft_claim: Rhetorical urgency is legitimate only when grounded in a real, modifiable exigence; inventing a deadline or looming catastrophe to intensify uplift is manipulation and is prohibited in this repository.

supporting_evidence.note: Bitzer defines a rhetorical exigence as an imperfection marked by urgency that discourse can modify, and makes the situation, not the rhetor's wish, the ground of rhetorical activity.

supporting_evidence.location: Address to the Constituent Assembly, 14-15 August 1947
supporting_evidence.note: Nehru's forward call is grounded in an actual, documented historical occasion, not an invented deadline; the urgency is inherited from the moment.

counterevidence.note: No counter-evidence located in this pass: the dossier records this as a repository-level prohibition (section G 'Urgency inflation') rather than an empirical finding, and card sections 4 and 7 supply only scope conditions (a real deadline routes to tone-urgent; fiction may render a false deadline as a character's error). No source in this silo argues that manufactured urgency is legitimate or that exigence-grounding is insufficient.

scope: All forms; a hard repository constraint rather than a stylistic preference.
exceptions: Where a genuine deadline or crisis exists, the tone-urgent surface takes over or the two alternate under the combination rules.
